paper_title: Torsion-balance tests of the weak equivalence principle
suggested_experiment_name: Eöt-Wash torsion-balance WEP test (Be-Ti and Be-Al)
coupling_convention: Dimensionless coupling strength |α̃| for Yukawa interaction coupled to B−L charge, as plotted on y-axis
notes: This paper presents WEP (weak equivalence principle) torsion-balance tests with Be-Ti and Be-Al test body pairs at part-in-10^13 precision. The results constrain Yukawa-type fifth forces and scalar interactions (dilaton couplings). However, the paper does NOT present exclusion limits in the standard (mass, coupling) format used for dark matter searches. Instead, it reports: (1) Eotvos parameters η and differential accelerations (Table 3); (2) Constraints on Yukawa strength α̃ vs range λ (Figure 6, left panel); (3) Constraints on dilaton couplings D_m̂ and D_e in parameter space (Figure 7); (4) Bounds on antimatter freefall (Figure 8); (5) Bounds on non-gravitational dark matter interactions (Figure 9). The coupling type is ScalarBaryon because the paper discusses scalar fifth forces coupling to baryon/nucleon mass and composition-dependent effects. However, no extractable (mass_eV, coupling) data points exist in standard form. The results are presented as constraints on Yukawa range λ (in meters, not eV) and on dimensionless dilaton coefficients. The paper is primarily a review/summary of WEP tests rather than a new dark matter search with conventional exclusion plots. Extraction confidence is low because: (1) no standard (m_a, g) exclusion curve; (2) coupling type is inferred from context (fifth forces, scalar interactions) rather than explicit dark matter coupling constants; (3) data are in non-standard formats (Eotvos parameters, Yukawa range constraints, dilaton parameter space). | selector: figure_vision (sole candidate) | Vision: Figure 6 (left panel) shows 95% CL upper bounds on the strength of a vector Yukawa interaction coupled to q̃ = B − L (baryon minus lepton number). The x-axis is range λ in meters (log scale, 10^-2 to 10^12 m). The y-axis is |α̃| in dimensionless coupling units (log scale, 10^-11 to 10^-5). The excluded region is ABOVE the boundary curves. The plot shows multiple constraint curves: EW (Eöt-Wash lab-fixed results from Be-Ti and Be-Al), EW94, EW99, Princeton, Moscow, and LLR (lunar laser-ranging). The lower boundary of the exclusion region follows the EW curve, which shows a characteristic dip around λ ~ 10^7 m (corresponding to ~10^-6 eV mass equivalent via λ = ℏc/m). The boundary rises steeply at both short and long ranges. Mass conversion: λ [m] ↔ m [eV] via m = 1.240e-6 eV·m / λ. At λ = 1 m, m ≈ 1.24e-6 eV; at λ = 10^7 m, m ≈ 1.24e-13 eV. The paper discusses implications for dark matter and antimatter interactions. This is a test of the weak equivalence principle (WEP) using torsion-balance methods, constraining composition-dependent fifth forces. | Calibration: No calibration needed
